Alex — thanks for the clear ask. Draft summary / strawman below; attaching an editable order form redline.

Strawman (high level):
- Inspection boundary: bounded, scheduled windows against a staging environment only; 48-hour notice for non-emergency requests. No direct production access.
- Pen test: allowed by third-party vendors with prior approval; tests limited to agreed IP ranges and credentials; 14-day rolling test window. We provide ephemeral test accounts and scoped logging.
- Evidence cadence: propose weekly artifact snapshot for onboarding (first 60 days) then biweekly cadence thereafter; critical control failures generate immediate notification and a one-week remediation follow-up.

I've attached draft_orderform_redlines.docx with inline language for the security exhibit. Monica, can you confirm the technical feasibility of ephemeral creds + log pulls on our side? Laura, looping you for legal redlines — Karthik will take the lead once you review.

Attachments: draft_orderform_redlines.docx (docx)

— Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

On Tue, May 12, 2027 at 11:03 AM dylan_brooks@redwood.com wrote:
> Strawman (high level):
> - Inspection boundary: bounded, scheduled windows against a staging environment only; 48-hour notice for non-emergency requests. No direct production access.

Thanks — quick legal read and proposed changes below (high level):

1) Narrow "inspection" to "evidence review and scheduled, timeboxed observation of staging artifacts". Avoid open-ended "inspection rights."
2) Pen test clause: allow third-party testing subject to (a) prior written approval of vendor, (b) mutually agreed scope and test window, (c) non-destructive testing only, and (d) a requirement that vendor coordinate through Redwood's security contact and sign our standard non-disclosure and rules-of-engagement addendum.
3) Evidence cadence: accept onboarding weekly snapshots for 60 days, then biweekly; add a clause limiting sample size to avoid disproportionate operational burden (e.g., sampling matrix in appendix).
4) SLA/credits: do not agree to credits tied to security findings; we can agree to remediation timelines and a joint remediation plan with escalation paths.

I'll produce a tracked redline of the MSA appendix and the order form security exhibit by EOD tomorrow. Laura — please confirm if procurement needs alternative wording for DocuSign routing.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Alex — quick pass on the tech ops side:
- Ephemeral credentials: we can issue time-limited staging credentials scoped to the test. Credentials will expire automatically after the agreed window.
- Logging & artifacts: we can provide weekly artifact snapshots (config, access logs, relevant KV cache slices) for the onboarding period; for sampling we recommend a matrix where high-risk services are sampled weekly and lower-risk services biweekly.
- Pen-test coordination: we require a rules-of-engagement doc and a single point of contact. For tests that may affect availability we prefer a maintenance window and a 72-hour pre-notice for destructive tests (destructive tests will not be allowed without explicit exception).

See attached pen-test-scope-diagram.png for proposed staging topology and sample artifact pull points.

Attachments: pen-test-scope-diagram.png (png)

I'll work with engineering to prepare a short operational runbook we can attach as an appendix to the order form.
